quote: except that the latter expresses the possibility of failure
content:
Ordinary language does not reveal the speaker’s objective function
Saying one will try often expresses uncertainty about success while retaining a serious intention to achieve it. The essay recognizes a colloquial use, but its rhetorical distinction should not become a diagnostic test of someone’s motives. Ask what actions, contingencies and feedback the person has planned.

quote: being satisfied with having a plan
content:
Concrete contingencies are the testable version
The distinction becomes useful when it changes behavior: identify the next action, the obstacle and what to do if that obstacle occurs. Research on implementation intentions gives this kind of if–then planning a measurable form. It supplies no evidence that changing one’s vocabulary or intensifying commitment alone improves outcomes.
Gollwitzer & Sheeran (2006)

quote: three times your life savings, and you
content:
A vivid stake does not eliminate opportunity cost
Maximizing one task’s probability of success is a narrower objective than using one’s resources well. Extra effort can impose unacceptable costs on other goals, even when the task matters greatly. A dramatic hypothetical reward focuses attention; it does not establish how much real-world effort is optimal.
